payload.title: Choose single-item ideas by signals, not by 'every accepted monitored undrafted Reference'
payload.description:
Ryan 11-01: single-item ideas keep running to find individual items worth a post, but they must be guided by data/signals.
In ideas/monitor_stories.py:
- Candidates: any accepted Reference with a sourceUri, monitored or not (drop the notMonitored rule; keep sameSource, excluded host, promoted, judgedNotRelevant, already-cited-by-an-idea rules). Pending References are not single-item candidates (they can't be evidence).
- Score each candidate with an item signal from S1.2 inputs: the Reference's own activity (human accept with reason, Messages on it, links to it, its concepts' acceptance surprise, Cyclotron probability) as a p-value/surprise on the same scale as packs (percentile against the site's own distribution, no thresholds).
- Interleave single-item candidates with packs in one queue ordered by surprise (S1.3 ranking); the run stops only on time/cost/file_error.
- Keep the single-item fetch and prompt as today.
Tests: a monitor-less accepted Reference with a lively thread outranks a quiet monitored one; a quiet site still files nothing rather than everything.
Gherkin scenarios for both.
Owner rules that apply: no fixed caps, day windows or magic thresholds (derive or learn them; bound only by time, cost, context size); decisions go to decision models (Jev / the site Cyclotron), the LLM (GPT-6 Luna) only writes; Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) for every behaviour change; say "idea(s)", never "draft"/"proposed story".
